newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED INCREASE BATISTUTA BID - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED INCREASE BATISTUTA BID - PAPER.

text.p: Manchester United have increased a bid for Fiorentina's Argentine captain Gabriel Batistuta to 35 billion lire ($21 million), an Italian newspaper reported on Saturday.
Gazzetta dello Sport said that United manager Alex Ferguson had sent a fax offering the sum in cash for a striker who has recently sounded increasingly unsettled.

The paper added that Internazionale president Massimo Moratti had offered more than 40 billion lire ($24 million) for the player. Inter's offer may be less likely to succeed because Fiorentina, who have insisted in the past that Batistuta is not for sale, have made quite clear that they would never let the player join an Italian rival.
But Gazzetta said Batistuta's manager Antonio Imborgia met Inter's Sandro Mazzola, the former Italian great who now deals with most of their transfers, on Friday.
Fiorentina general manager Luciano Luna said several clubs were chasing Batistuta but Fiorentina were determined to keep him.
"But we have never been contacted. No-one has approached us officially," he said.
